p.x:
What if every elementary particle is actually a cyclic machine?
It can be tested through predictions and experiments.
It could be the Next Huge Thing.
Machine consists of a list of instructions. Each instruction represents some direction in space: left, right, up, down, forward, back. Machine executes all it's states one after another and moves in corresponding direction of space the same discrete distance on each tick of time. After some state is executed, control is passed to the next state. It happens infinitely in a loop. After last state is executed, control is passed to the first state.
So machine moves and moves until it's state is changed.
https://t.co/FPtDIbX971
Properties and phenomena that this machine reproduces:
- E - total energy: total amount of states. Energy of one state is numerically equal to reduced Planck’s constant and is the reason why action is discrete
- inertia (First Newton's Law): Machine keeps on moving infinitely until it's state is updated and the more states in machine the more states to be updated and the more particle "resists to acceleration"
https://t.co/eFpJ6OARva
- limited speed: you can not move faster than straight - discrete action (interaction): change in energy equals energy of one state
- reduced wave length: contribution of one discrete piece in motion
https://t.co/oAVspagPZy
- uncertainty and observer effect: interaction destroys the original particle so you can't know some properties of the particle after interaction. Because you can't control, which state will be taken from machine or passed to machine
https://t.co/pJqVk8jUHu
- momentum and conservation of momentum: amount of states that represents motion
https://t.co/OH0jlQptzi
- rest mass: amount of states that represents cyclic motion. For example a pair of states left-right does not move machine anywhere, but takes ticks of time to be executed. 
- speed: If you have particle RRRR, it moves with maximum possible speed right. If you have RRRRLLL, it moves right 1 moment of time out of 7. So it's average speed is 1/7 of the maximum speed
- Photons generated by set of particles have more or less the same speed in any direction https://t.co/NysURFlSWO
- Discrete rules lead to circular motion and "wave behaviour":
https://t.co/LIRj9C3q4M
and more.
Bell inequalities say nothing about locality. They show that interaction destroys hidden variables, therefor hidden variables can not be "measured".
https://t.co/TtCgcpkE9v

p.x:
Slides from my talk yesterday.

Here is what this represents. I'm trying to describe and model how DMT visuals come about within a paradigm of non-linear optics (cf. electromagnetic theories of consciousness). On high dose DMT it often feels like you experience a world where "everything reflects everything else". You might be looking at a statue made of eyes and within each eye there is a weirdly contorted version of the whole scene. These parts somehow are both one and many at the same time. At the limit the system is fully interlocked on multiple levels and it acts as a coherent multi-level organism. Whats going on here? 

We start with the cel animation model of visual rendering: our visual field literally uses a kind of cel animation system where 'stickers' of sorts are added to different parts of the visual field to populate a scene. Each 'sticker' can be edited independently of each other and yet can interact with the others. 

What I propose is the brain can generate these cel animation elements using information about the shape of the entire experience. In other words, the holistic information available to the witness of the whole scene can itself influence the meaning and texture of each of the cel animation elements.

I think this might be implemented, at its core, with a circuit such as the one I drew below:

The happy face represents the image fed to the visual field. The weird white rocks represent TV stones, which beam this image to separate independent modules. Then we get to the layer of non-linear optics. Akin to a neural network but for non-linear optical operations on the image, each module passes its own version of the field through a network of filters. The weight of the filters determines their presence and interaction with the image - this is presumably modulated "classically" by neurons adjusting the instantaneous contribution of each operation.

There are two time scales. The time scales of neurons, which adjust the elements, and the time scales of light circulating around the circuit. 

The image is then reconstructed (for each module), which in practice results in a version of the screen that has been altered. The alteration is effectively a stack of non-linear optical transformations, but functionally might result in "enhanced edges" or "without the colors" or "highlight the facial features". Each of these reconstructed images is then passed through a symmetry group filter that applies symmetrical transformations to the reconstructed image in order to 'project' it back onto the original screen.

This process is instantaneously repeated: after all it's an image going through a complicated system of non-linear optical filters. The resulting experience is the point of stability of this process. It has a vibe; as a standing wave pattern it can equally be described in terms of phases and frequencies as it can in terms of spatial distribution.

What's the upshot?

This sort of basic core architecture can reconstruct Indra's Net and countless other DMT phenomenology. At least conceptually, if not in practice. Each of the holograms projected back into the original screen is itself an image of the screen as a whole after a number of filters and transformations. More so, on the screen itself the images can interact, and literally "drag" each other.

That's how you can interact with a 7 dimensional being on DMT. Effectively interacting with cel animation elements with a depth of recursion that can collectively tune into much more intricate mathematical orders than we usually experience. The state-space of this kind of phenomenology resembles more a state-space of possible fractals than something as simple as pressure and temperature (though those are there too).

p.x:
When asked to speak without exaggeration about AI advancements over the next 12 months, Demis Hassabis(@demishassabis) highlighted the following three points:

1. A lot of progress in multimodality: We are currently gaining very interesting synergy effects as models become multimodal. A recent example of this is "Nano Banana Pro." In particular, as video and language models combine next year, we will see a very interesting combination of capabilities.

2. Advancement of 'World Models': The development of models such as Genie-3.

3. Reliable Agents: While the industry has discussed agents extensively this year, they are not yet able to complete entire tasks perfectly and reliably. However, he thinks that by next year, we will have agents that come very close to that level.
